ios._supportsTablet_comment: 2026-09-15: iPad is a first-class target. Expo's withRequiresFullScreen plugin writes all four UISupportedInterfaceOrientations~ipad values because requireFullScreen is unset; orientation:'portrait' above still locks the PHONE. Do not add the ~ipad key by hand. Layout: proto css/wide.css.
ios._appleTeamId_comment: Read out of ios-certs/appstore.mobileprovision. @bacons/apple-targets needs it to sign the widget extension it generates.
ios._entitlements_comment: The App Group the Live Activity card and the app share. Named HERE and only here: @bacons/apple-targets mirrors this array into every target that can use App Groups, so the widget extension inherits it without repeating the string. It must match RollCallPendingStore.suiteName in modules/rollcall-live/ios/RollCallCheckInIntent.swift, and a group that the provisioning profile does not carry fails code-signing. time-sensitive: the roll call backup alert (v3), the start push for an athlete with no armed alarm (commitment-reminders openingDelivery). The capability is on the App ID via scripts/apple-provision.mjs --time-sensitive, and ios-certs/appstore.mobileprovision must be re-minted in the same run: a profile without it fails code-signing. It needs no Info.plist purpose string.
ios._infoPlist_microphone_comment: Dictation in the chat composer (2026-09-23): the ONE microphone string in the build. expo-speech-recognition, expo-camera and expo-image-picker all write NSMicrophoneUsageDescription; none of them is given its own value, so each keeps this one instead of Expo's 'Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to access your microphone' placeholder (the plugins only fall back to the placeholder when this key is empty). Verify with npx expo config --type introspect.

infoPlist.NSCameraUsageDescription: OnStandard uses the camera so you can photograph a meal and get instant nutrition feedback. Photos are analyzed for your log only.
infoPlist.NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription: OnStandard needs photo library access so you can pick an existing meal photo to log and analyze.
infoPlist.NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription: OnStandard saves a share card you create to your photos when you choose Save.
infoPlist.NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription: OnStandard uses your location to check you in when you arrive where your coach asked you to be, and to center the map when a coach sets that place. Your location is only checked against that place. Your coach sees only whether you arrived, never where you are.
infoPlist.NSLocationAlwaysAndWhenInUseUsageDescrip: So your arrival counts even when the app is closed, OnStandard checks you in when you walk into the place your coach set, only during the check-in window. Your coach sees only whether you arrived, never where you are.
infoPlist.NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription: So your arrival counts even when the app is closed, OnStandard checks you in when you walk into the place your coach set, only during the check-in window. Your coach sees only whether you arrived, never where you are.
infoPlist.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: OnStandard uses the microphone only when you tap the mic in a chat, so you can say your message instead of typing it. Nothing is recorded or kept: your words become text you can edit before you send.
infoPlist.NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription: When you tap the mic in a chat, OnStandard turns what you say into text in the message box. It works on your device when it can; otherwise your voice goes to Apple's speech service to be turned into text. Nothing is sent to anyone until you check the text and tap Send.

privacyManifests._NSPrivacyCollectedDataTypes_comment: Was an empty array, which declares 'this app collects nothing' — false, and a known rejection/removal trigger. Each entry below was traced to a real column or table, not assumed. Tracking is false throughout: there are no ad, attribution or third-party analytics SDKs, so there is no ATT prompt. PRECISE LOCATION is declared as of 2026-09-23 (founder: the arrival check-in returns). It was deliberately NOT declared while arrival was judged on the device and only a verdict crossed the wire, and not at all after the feature was removed on 2026-09-09 (8e7506bb). Since 0242 the phone sends at most ONE position reading per arrival (a region Enter, which may send none when iOS refuses a background fix, or an 'I'm here' tap) to verify_arrival_at, inside the athlete's signed-in request; the server measures the distance to the coach's place, stores the verdict (and 'Not at <place>' on a miss; the distance goes back to the athlete in that reply and is never stored) against the athlete, and does not keep the coordinate. That is declared as Precise Location, LINKED (it is sent with the athlete's identity and its verdict is stored on their row; 'not linked' would claim identifiers were stripped first, which they are not), NOT tracking, App Functionality only. Apple's own definition of 'collect' (kept longer than needed to service the request in real time) could arguably exclude a discarded reading; declaring it is the conservative and defensible answer, and App Store Connect's App Privacy answers must say the same thing. PURCHASES will need adding the day Stripe or IAP starts charging. FOUNDER: this is a legal attestation — confirm it against docs/go-live/APP-STORE-SETUP.md before you submit.

plugins._comment: 2026-09-23: the app DOES use the microphone now, for dictation in the chat composer (expo-speech-recognition, below). Until then microphonePermission was false here and on expo-image-picker, because nothing recorded audio and both plugins inject Expo's placeholder mic string ('Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to access your microphone'), a 5.1.1 rejection on its own. Neither plugin is given a mic string now: each keeps ios.infoPlist.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription, the one real string. Do NOT set microphonePermission:false again: it DELETES that key (the speech module would then crash the app on the first tap of the mic), and on expo-image-picker it also BLOCKS android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO, which Android dictation needs. recordAudioAndroid stays false: the camera never records audio; RECORD_AUDIO comes from the speech plugin. Verify with npx expo config --type introspect.
plugins.cameraPermission: OnStandard uses the camera so you can photograph a meal and get instant nutrition feedback. Photos are analyzed for your log only.

plugins._comment: Roll call v3 backup alert: the 28 s alarm tone the start push names for an athlete whose phone has no armed alarm (commitment-reminders openingDelivery, BACKUP_SOUND). Generated by scripts/make-rollcall-sound.mjs (--check verifies it). A notification sound is part of the BINARY: an OTA cannot add it, and an older build plays the default sound for this name. No mode: aps-environment stays what it was (development; the distribution profile decides at export). enableBackgroundRemoteNotifications stays unset: it would add UIBackgroundModes, which app.config.test.ts forbids.

Dictation in every chat composer (2026-09-23). No purpose strings here on purpose: the plugin keeps ios.infoPlist's NSMicrophoneUsageDescription and NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription when it is given none, so each string lives in one place. It adds android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO and the <queries> entry for Google's recognition service. The native module ships with a BINARY; the proto hides the mic on any build without it (bridge DICTATION_AVAILABLE).

backgroundColor is the app canvas (--bg #070B14), not the old brand blue. Launch used to flash a full screen of #1E50D6 and then cut to a near-black app, which is the single most visible 'unfinished' moment in the product because it happens every single open. Dark splash -> dark canvas -> the ring draws itself. NOTE: a splash change is native config, so it ships with the next BINARY, never over OTA.

Arrival check-in, restored 2026-09-23. isIosBackgroundLocationEnabled is FALSE on purpose: it would add UIBackgroundModes location, which is exactly what App Review rejected under 2.5.4 on 2026-09-18 ('unable to locate any features that require persistent location'). Region monitoring does not need it: the OS watches the coach's place and wakes the app. 'Always' is still requested because region monitoring needs it. If iOS refuses a reading in that wake, the app reports the region match without one (0242 section 5b). app.config.test.ts fails if the mode comes back. Every purpose string is set here on purpose: the plugin writes Expo's placeholder 'Allow $(PRODUCT_NAME) to access your location' into any key left empty, including the legacy NSLocationAlwaysUsageDescription, and a placeholder motion string when motionUsagePermission is empty. motionUsagePermission is a real, true string (not false): expo-location links CoreMotion, and App Store Connect refused build 44 with ITMS-90683 for the missing NSMotionUsageDescription. The app reads no motion data and never asks for it.

plugins._comment: Wake-Up Roll Call lock screen. appGroup is set now that group.com.onstandard.app exists on both App IDs and both provisioning profiles carry it (verified 2026-09-02). It is idempotent with the ios.entitlements array above; both converge on the same list.

READ ONLY, and deliberately minimal. The plugin turns background-delivery ON by default and writes an UPDATE usage string by default. background:false still stands. The UPDATE string was `false` until 2026-09-02, on the principle that declaring a permission the app never uses is dishonest and an App Review flag. App Store Connect now REJECTS THE UPLOAD without it: 'EAS_UPLOAD_TO_ASC_MISSING_PURPOSE_STRING ... Missing keys reported by App Store Connect: NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription'. That is what had kept TestFlight on build 26 since 2026-08-20 — build #27 was the first with HealthKit and was never submitted, so nobody found out. The string now says plainly that the app never writes, which keeps the honesty and satisfies the validator. OnStandard never writes to Health and never reads in the background, so declaring either would be asking for a permission the app does not use, which is both dishonest and an App Review flag. background:false also keeps com.apple.developer.healthkit.background-delivery out of the entitlements, so the provisioning profile only has to carry com.apple.developer.healthkit.
plugins.NSHealthShareUsageDescription: OnStandard reads last night's sleep, heart rate variability and resting heart rate to give your recovery check-in real context. If your coach sets an activity standard, it also reads your steps, walking and running distance, exercise minutes, active energy and workouts, and your coach sees your progress toward that standard. Nothing is ever written to Health.
plugins.NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription: OnStandard never writes to Apple Health. It only reads, with your permission, for your recovery check-in and any activity standard your coach sets.
